[Molecule: Arginine], [Arginine (Arg, R) is a positively charged amino acid with molecular formula C6H14N4O2 and molar mass 174.20 g/mol. Its guanidinium side chain has pKa 12.48. [Molecule: Asparagine], [Asparagine (Asn, N) is a polar amino acid with molecular formula C4H8N2O3 and molar mass 132.12 g/mol. It was the first amino acid to be isolated (from asparagus in 1806). [Molecule: Aspartate], [Aspartate (aspartic acid, Asp, D) is a negatively charged amino acid with molecular formula C4H7NO4 and molar mass 133.10 g/mol. Its side chain carboxyl group has pKa 3.65. [ Aspirin (C₉H₈O₄) ], [ Acetylsalicylic acid. A common analgesic and anti-inflammatory. ]

[ Ethane ], [ A two-carbon alkane. A colorless, odorless gas. ]

[Molecule: Calcium Chloride], [Calcium chloride (CaCl2) is an ionic compound with molar mass 110.98 g/mol. [Molecule: Carbon Monoxide], [Carbon monoxide (CO) is a colourless, odourless, toxic gas with molar mass 28.01 g/mol. It is produced by incomplete combustion of carbon-containing fuels. [Molecule: Cellulose], [Cellulose is a polysaccharide consisting of linear chains of beta-1,4-linked glucose units. [Molecule: Adenine], [Adenine is a purine nucleobase with molecular formula C5H5N5. It is one of the four nucleobases in DNA (pairs with thymine) and RNA (pairs with uracil). [Molecule: Ethanol], [Ethanol (ethyl alcohol, C2H5OH) is a volatile, flammable liquid with molar mass 46.07 g/mol. It is produced by fermentation of sugars by yeast. [ Formaldehyde ], [ Methanal. The simplest aldehyde. A toxic gas with a pungent smell. ]
[ Fructose ], [ Fruit sugar. A ketonic monosaccharide isomer of glucose. ]

[Molecule: Glutamate], [Glutamate (glutamic acid, Glu, E) is a negatively charged amino acid with molecular formula C5H9NO4 and molar mass 147.13 g/mol. [Molecule: Glutamine], [Glutamine (Gln, Q) is a polar amino acid with molecular formula C5H10N2O3 and molar mass 146.15 g/mol. It is the most abundant free amino acid in the blood. [ Histidine (C₆H₉N₃O₂) ], [ An essential amino acid with an imidazole functional group. ]

[Molecule: Hydrochloric Acid], [Hydrochloric acid (HCl in solution) is a strong mineral acid produced by dissolving hydrogen chloride gas in water. Molar mass of HCl: 36.46 g/mol. [Molecule: Hydrogen Fluoride], [Hydrogen fluoride (HF) is a colourless gas or liquid with molar mass 20.01 g/mol. It is a weak acid in dilute solution but highly corrosive and toxic. [Molecule: Hydrogen Gas], [Dihydrogen (H2) is the lightest and most abundant molecule in the universe. Molar mass 2.016 g/mol. It is a colourless, odourless, highly flammable gas. [ Hydrogen Peroxide ], [ A pale blue liquid, slightly more viscous than water. Strong oxidizer. ]

[Molecule: Hydrogen Sulfide], [Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) is a colourless, flammable gas with the characteristic smell of rotten eggs. Molar mass 34.08 g/mol. [Molecule: Iron(III) Oxide], [Iron(III) oxide (Fe2O3, haematite, rust) is the most common iron oxide with molar mass 159.69 g/mol. It is the main component of rust and the mineral haematite. [Molecule: Isoleucine], [Isoleucine (Ile, I) is a nonpolar essential amino acid with molecular formula C6H13NO2 and molar mass 131.17 g/mol. [Molecule: Leucine], [Leucine (Leu, L) is a nonpolar essential amino acid with molecular formula C6H13NO2 and molar mass 131.17 g/mol. It is the most abundant branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) and a key regulator of protein synthesis via the mTOR pathway. Leucine is essential for muscle protein synthesis and is found in high concentrations in meat, dairy, and legumes.]

[Molecule: Lysine], [Lysine (Lys, K) is a positively charged essential amino acid with molecular formula C6H14N2O2 and molar mass 146.19 g/mol. Its long side chain ends in an amino group (pKa 10.53). [Molecule: Magnesium Oxide], [Magnesium oxide (MgO, magnesia) is a white crystalline solid with molar mass 40.30 g/mol. [Molecule: Methane], [Methane (CH4) is the simplest alkane and the primary component of natural gas. Molar mass 16.04 g/mol. [ Methanol ], [ Wood alcohol. The simplest alcohol. Toxic solvent and fuel. ]

[Molecule: Methionine], [Methionine (Met, M) is a nonpolar essential amino acid with molecular formula C5H11NO2S and molar mass 149.21 g/mol. It contains a thioether group in its side chain. [Molecule: Sodium Chloride], [Table salt. An ionic compound forming a cubic crystal lattice.]
[ Nitric Acid ], [ A highly corrosive mineral acid. Used in fertilizers and explosives. ]

[Molecule: Nitrogen Dioxide], [Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is a reddish-brown toxic gas with molar mass 46.01 g/mol. It is a major air pollutant produced by combustion engines and lightning. [Molecule: Potassium Chloride], [Potassium chloride (KCl) is an ionic compound with molar mass 74.55 g/mol. It is a white crystalline solid highly soluble in water. [Molecule: Proline], [Proline (Pro, P) is a cyclic amino acid with molecular formula C5H9NO2 and molar mass 115.13 g/mol. Its side chain is bonded back to the amino group, forming a pyrrolidine ring. [Molecule: Ribose], [D-Ribose is a pentose monosaccharide with molecular formula C5H10O5. It is the sugar component of RNA, ATP, NAD+, and FAD. Ribose is produced in the pentose phosphate pathway. Unlike deoxyribose (in DNA), ribose has a hydroxyl group at the 2-prime carbon position.]

[Molecule: Serine], [Serine (Ser, S) is a polar amino acid with molecular formula C3H7NO3 and molar mass 105.09 g/mol. [Molecule: Silicon Dioxide], [Silicon dioxide (SiO2, silica, quartz) is the most abundant mineral in the Earth's crust with molar mass 60.08 g/mol. [Molecule: Sodium Bicarbonate], [Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3, baking soda, bicarbonate of soda) is a white crystalline solid with molar mass 84.007 g/mol. [Molecule: Starch], [Starch is a polysaccharide consisting of alpha-1,4-linked glucose units (amylose) and alpha-1,6-branched chains (amylopectin). [Molecule: Sucrose], [Sucrose (table sugar) is a disaccharide composed of glucose and fructose linked by a glycosidic bond. Molecular formula C12H22O11, molar mass 342.30 g/mol. [ Sulfuric Acid ], [ A strong mineral acid. Highly corrosive and hygroscopic. ]

[Molecule: Sulfur Dioxide], [Sulfur dioxide (SO2) is a colourless, toxic gas with a pungent smell and molar mass 64.06 g/mol. It is produced by burning sulfur-containing fuels and volcanic eruptions. [Molecule: Threonine], [Threonine (Thr, T) is a polar essential amino acid with molecular formula C4H9NO3 and molar mass 119.12 g/mol. It has both hydroxyl and methyl groups on its side chain. [Molecule: Water], [Water (H2O) is the universal solvent and the most abundant liquid on Earth's surface. Molar mass 18.015 g/mol. [Particle: Electron], [The electron is a stable first-generation lepton with charge -1 and mass 0.511 MeV. [Particle: Muon], [The muon is a second-generation lepton with charge -1 and mass 105.66 MeV, approximately 207 times heavier than the electron. [Particle: Muon Neutrino], [The muon neutrino is a second-generation neutral lepton with mass <0.17 MeV. It is produced in muon decay and pion decay. Muon neutrinos interact only via the weak force. Symbol: nu_mu. They participate in neutrino oscillations with electron and tau neutrinos.]

[Particle: Positron], [The positron is the antiparticle of the electron. It has charge +1, mass 0.511 MeV, and spin 1/2. When a positron meets an electron they annihilate, producing two gamma-ray photons each of 0.511 MeV. Positrons are produced in beta-plus decay and pair production. Symbol: e+.]

[Particle: Proton], [The proton is a stable baryon composed of two up quarks and one down quark (uud), bound by the strong force via gluons. It has charge +1, mass 938.272 MeV, and spin 1/2. [Particle: Bottom Quark], [The bottom quark (also called the beauty quark) is a third-generation quark with charge -1/3 and mass ~4180 MeV. It carries bottom quantum number -1. Bottom quarks appear in B mesons and bottom baryons. Discovered in 1977 at Fermilab in the Upsilon meson.]

[Particle: Charm Quark], [The charm quark is a second-generation quark with charge +2/3 and mass ~1275 MeV. It carries charm quantum number +1. Charm quarks appear in D mesons and charmed baryons. Discovered in 1974 in the J/psi meson.]

[Particle: Down Quark], [The down quark is a first-generation quark with charge -1/3 and mass ~4.7 MeV. Together with the up quark it forms the lightest quark doublet. Down quarks are constituents of protons (uud) and neutrons (udd). They carry colour charge and interact via the strong force.]

[Particle: Strange Quark], [The strange quark is a second-generation quark with charge -1/3 and mass ~95 MeV. It carries strangeness quantum number -1. Strange quarks appear in kaons and hyperons. They are heavier than up and down quarks and decay via the weak force.]

[Particle: Top Quark], [The top quark is the heaviest known elementary particle with mass ~172760 MeV (172.76 GeV). It is a third-generation quark with charge +2/3. [Particle: Up Quark], [The up quark is a first-generation quark with charge +2/3 and mass ~2.2 MeV. It is one of the two lightest quarks and a constituent of protons (uud) and neutrons (udd). Up quarks carry colour charge and interact via the strong nuclear force through gluon exchange.]

It operates at 400-500 degrees C and 150-300 bar pressure using an iron catalyst. It is the most important industrial chemical reaction, producing ~150 million tonnes of ammonia per year for fertilisers. It consumes ~1-2% of global energy.]

[Reaction: Nuclear Fission of U-235], [Nuclear fission of uranium-235 occurs when a neutron is absorbed: U-235 + n → Ba-141 + Kr-92 + 3n + 200 MeV. The three released neutrons can trigger further fissions (chain reaction). This reaction is the basis of nuclear power plants and atomic bombs. It releases ~200 MeV per fission, approximately 50 million times more energy than chemical combustion.]

[Reaction: Nuclear Fusion D-T], [Deuterium-tritium fusion: D + T → He-4 + n + 17.6 MeV. This is the most energetically favourable fusion reaction at achievable temperatures (~100 million K). It is the basis of hydrogen bombs and the target reaction for fusion energy research (ITER, NIF). Deuterium is abundant in seawater; tritium is produced from lithium-6.]

The overall equation is: 6CO2 + 6H2O + light → C6H12O6 + 6O2. It occurs in two stages: the light reactions (in the thylakoid membrane) and the Calvin cycle (in the stroma). Photosynthesis is the primary source of oxygen in Earth's atmosphere.]
